description: Terrain heights on the cost grid. elevation_grid.bin holds the layers below one after another, each rows x cols little-endian int16 in row-major order (index = row * cols + col; row 0 = northern edge, col 0 = western edge). Metres = value * scale; nodata means no data.
source: NASA Mars Trek: MRO CTX Jezero DEM (Controlled), 20 m
vertical_datum: Height 0 is the Mars areoid (MOLA topography): the USGS file name is JEZ_ctx_B_soc_008_DTM_MOLAtopography_DeltaGeoid_20m, and the landing site reads about -2,567 m, Jezero's known floor level. USGS's processing note says the intermediate CTX DTMs referred to the Mars 2000 sphere (R = 3396190 m); heights on that sphere would be about 1-2 km lower here.
vertical_accuracy: USGS: vertical registration between the CTX DTMs is 3.8 m after aligning the mosaic to the HRSC DTM (whose vertical precision is about 13 m); Mars 2020 TRN required < 20 m. Source: USGS metadata for doi:10.5066/P906QQT8.

layers.name: elevation_m
layers.description: mean height of the cell's 2 x 2 DEM pixels

layers.name: min_m
layers.description: lowest of the cell's 2 x 2 DEM pixels

layers.name: max_m
layers.description: highest of the cell's 2 x 2 DEM pixels

layers.name: relief_m
layers.description: elevation_m minus the mean elevation_m of the 7 x 7 cells around the cell (~280 m x 266 m, the cell itself left out; smaller near the border): + = stands above its surroundings (mound, ridge, crater rim), - = lies below them (pit, crater floor, channel)
